**Causality** — causation and the structure of causal relations — causal order, definite and indefinite, and its combinatorics, topology and geometry; sheaf- and process-theoretic accounts of causality; causal models, causal inference and interventionist accounts of what a causal relation is; and the metaphysics of causation — exclusion, mental causation, causal emergence and closure, reciprocal causation (ADR-035).

| [THEORY-058](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-058.md) v2 | Mental disorders are maintained by self-reinforcing causal loops rather than expressing a latent common cause, which is how they can outlast their triggers | Three traditions that do not cite one another for it put self-sustaining loops where a latent cause would be. Borsboom ([LIT-547](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-547.md)) makes disorder an alternative stable state of a strongly connected symptom network, kept up by hysteresis after its trigger has gone. Salkovskis, Sighvatsson and Sigurdsson ([LIT-538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-538.md)) make it a threat meaning protected by the behaviour it drives. Kendler ([LIT-539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-539.md)) finds causal loops across levels, from genes to culture. It says nothing about what starts a disorder. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-133](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-133.md) v2 | In List and Menzies's account of causes as difference-makers, a higher-level property that makes a difference to an effect is its cause, and its realizer is not, exactly when in some nearest situation without that realizer the property is realized differently and the effect still occurs; which holds depends on each causal system's counterfactual structure, not on levels a priori | List & Menzies (2009), [LIT-722](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-722.md). Take causes to be difference-makers. Then Kim's exclusion principle fails, and a revised one holds or fails system by system. Given that a higher-level property makes a difference to an effect, its realizer is not a cause exactly when some nearest situation without the realizer has the property realized otherwise and the effect present; the record re-derived this. The claim that higher-level relations are typically insensitive to their realizers is an observation about scientific practice, and Pernu disputes the paper's main example. | [THEORY-138](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-138.md) | X is a cause of Y exactly when some intervention on X with respect to Y would change Y, where an intervention is an exogenous causal process that alone sets X (M1), affects Y only through X (M2), is not caused by anything that affects Y by another route (M3), and leaves Y's causes off the path through X unchanged (M4); so defined, causation is not reduced to non-causal facts but is not viciously circular, and needs no human agent | Woodward, "Causation and Manipulability" (SEP, 2001; revised 2023), [LIT-713](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-713.md). A cause is what changes the effect under a surgical, exogenous intervention, defined relative to the effect by M1–M4. The account separates total from direct causes by combining interventions, and treats natural experiments as interventions. Active as the standard the record uses for what a causal claim asserts. This statement says nothing about invariance, proportionality or levels. | Active |
| [THEORY-171](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-171.md) v3 | When the causal constraints on events depend on context, deterministic assignments that are causal in each context can fail to glue into one causal assignment, so causal structure is itself a source of contextuality | From Gogioso & Pinzani's trilogy: The Topology of Causality, [LIT-808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-808.md), read in [NOTE-612](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-612.md), with the definitions of The Combinatorics of Causality, [LIT-800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-800.md) ([NOTE-635](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-635.md)). Over a space of input histories with the lowerset topology, causal functions form a separated presheaf, and on the space Θ₃ it is not a sheaf: two causal assignments on disjoint opens give one event two outputs on their common extension. That example was checked here, and it settles the claim. The source's Theorem 2.34, that the presheaf is a sheaf exactly when no two contexts impose incompatible causal pasts on a common event, is reported as the source's. Its proof was not read, and it is QUESTION-143. It does not say any physical or quantum data display the effect. | Active |
| [THEORY-177](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-177.md) v2 | In a binary cyclic system, the Contextuality-by-Default measure of signalling is twice the sum, over contents, of the least direct influence of context that a canonical causal model of the data must place on each content, and each content's least influence is the total-variation distance between its two marginals | Wang, Sadrzadeh, Abramsky & Cervantes (2021), [LIT-851](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-851.md), Proposition 1. | [THEORY-222](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-222.md) v4 | With uniform interventions imposed separately at each level, a coarse-grained macro description of a known discrete mechanism can have more effective information than the micro description it supervenes on, so the level at which effective information is highest can be a macro level | Hoel, Albantakis & Tononi (2013), [LIT-1038](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1038.md), read in [NOTE-726](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-726.md). | [THEORY-275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-275.md) v4 | In two optically trapped beads with a symmetric hydrodynamic coupling, one trap moved by a recorded noise drive, time-delayed mutual information and transfer entropy follow the drive's path rather than the coupling's symmetry: the flow between the beads reads two-way under moderate drive, in experiment and numerics, and one-way under strong drive, in numerics of the fitted model only | Das, Manikandan and Banerjee (2025), [LIT-947](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-947.md), read in [NOTE-788](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-788.md). | [THEORY-451](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-451.md) | A singular causal claim, that C will contribute or did contribute to E in a particular setting, is warranted only by joint evidence on each step of the causal process there, its causal principle, its support factors and the absence of its derailers, which no single method supplies; a well-run RCT secures at most the study population's average effect, and often not even that rigorously, and its result is not by its method evidence about any other population | Cartwright (2021), [LIT-213](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-213.md), read in [NOTE-161](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-161.md). | [THEORY-485](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-485.md) | Wave-function realism falsifies causal closure restricted to spacetime but is compatible with closure relative to fundamental physics, so quantum ontology opens no causal gap for non-physical causes; what it forces on the physicalist is a criterion of the physical and a bridge from dynamical to causal completeness | Poltorak (2026), [LIT-164](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-164.md), an unrefereed preprint read in full in [NOTE-112](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-112.md). "Every physical effect has a sufficient physical cause" has two tacit parameters, a domain and a completeness relation. With the domain set to spacetime the principle fails under wave-function realism; with it set to the ontology of a complete fundamental theory it survives. The move to a breach needs a premise that wave-function realists deny. The conclusions are modest and close to analytic once the terms are defined. The target is conceded to be a picture, not a published argument, and the dynamical-to-causal bridge is asserted, not argued. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-491](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-491.md) | Of the five standard arguments that randomisation gives a clinical trial special evidential weight, only the selection-bias argument is sound, and it supports only taking allocation out of the experimenters' hands; given balance on plausible confounders, a placebo or active control and blinding, randomisation is argued to add nothing, since balance on unknown confounders is not even probable in the one division a trial makes | Worrall (2007), [LIT-175](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-175.md), read in [NOTE-126](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-126.md). | [THEORY-710](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-710.md) | In a finite causal Bayesian network, a set of nodes is causally independent of another, imposing a third, for every choice of mechanisms exactly when every directed path between them passes through the third; information flow, conditional mutual information computed from interventional instead of observational distributions, vanishes under causal independence, and it can differ from transfer entropy and conditional mutual information in either direction | Ay & Polani (2008), [LIT-1174](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1174.md), read in full in [NOTE-946](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-946.md) from the 2006 preprint. Theorem 2 and Prop. 3 are proved; Examples 3–6 were recomputed. Example 6's one bit holds at k = 1 and fails for k ≥ 2 as stated. The measure needs the mechanisms, and estimation and identification are not addressed. | Active |
| [THEORY-711](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-711.md) | Directed information from an input sequence to an output sequence, the sum over time of the information the inputs up to now carry about the current output given the past outputs, is at most their mutual information and equal to it when the channel is used without feedback; in a causal system it bounds what the output reveals about the source, so feedback cannot raise a memoryless channel's capacity; and the usual definition of a memoryless channel holds only without feedback | Massey (1990), [LIT-1166](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1166.md), read in full in [NOTE-939](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-939.md) from the author's preprint. Three short theorems, all checked; the feedback inequality also checked numerically. "Causal" is Massey's factorization condition, not intervention. That directed information is full-history transfer entropy plus instantaneous terms is the record's derivation. | Active |
| [THEORY-764](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-764.md) | For a deterministic supervenient feature V of a Markov system, Rosas et al.'s practical emergence criterion Ψ equals the parts' whole-minus-sum information about V's next value minus V's one-step dynamical dependence I(V_t′; X_t \| V_t), so dynamical independence raises Ψ but neither implies emergence nor is implied by it, and the paper's sufficient test for causal decoupling can pass a feature that is not dynamically independent | Rosas et al. (2020), [LIT-1244](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1244.md), read in [NOTE-987](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-987.md), with Barnett and Seth's dynamical independence ([LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md), [THEORY-257](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-257.md)). By the chain rule, Ψ(V) = [I(X_t;V_t′) − Σ_j I(Xʲ_t;V_t′)] − I(V_t′;X_t\|V_t). The subtracted term vanishing implies Barnett–Seth independence for Markov X. Examples show each condition without the other. The independent sum of AR(1) channels has both, with no interaction. The identity concerns Ψ, the paper's practical criterion; it says nothing about the PID quantities themselves. | Active |
| [THEORY-787](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-787.md) | A system's causal structure can be most effective at a macro scale, so that causation emerges at a coarse-grained level and the macro description is the one at which the system's causes are found, as Hoel, Albantakis and Tononi propose from effective information | Hoel, Albantakis and Tononi (2013), [LIT-1038](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1038.md), argue that macro can beat micro: the scale at which effective information peaks is where a system's causal structure is, so causation can emerge at a macro level. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-222](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-222.md), only the arithmetic: under uniform interventions imposed separately at each level, a macro description can have more effective information. This is the causal thesis, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-801](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-801.md) | Agents are the systems that would adapt their policy were their actions to affect the world differently, so the agent is wherever that adaptation is: a thermostat is not an agent while it together with its design process is, an RL training process is while its learnt policy generally is not, and humans are | The definition and verdicts [THEORY-527](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-527.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit (batch 055) narrowed it to the recovery theorem. Kenton, Kumar, Farquhar, Richens, MacDermott and Everitt (2022), [LIT-909](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-909.md), propose the definition and argue the verdicts from it in §1 and §4; that it "reliably classifies humans as agents" is asserted. The verdicts are relative to the variables chosen, which the paper states. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-802](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-802.md) | In trained networks as in constructed ones, interchange interventions on a fixed set of variables can be satisfied equally by alignments related by a change of basis, so which internal direction mediates a high-level variable is fixed only relative to a chosen decomposition into units, and complex models will generally have several distinct, fully correct abstractions | The general reading that [THEORY-243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-243.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the three-unit network it proves (batch 062). Wu et al. (2024), [LIT-961](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-961.md), conjecture that complex models have "multiple distinct fully correct abstractions" and that the causal-abstraction framework cannot settle structural equivalence; Makelov et al. (2023), [LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md), §8, grant that crossing component boundaries makes "illusory" tenuous, and answer by privileging components. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. Its only support is the constructed tie. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-820](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-820.md) | For a stationary discrete-valued process X and any coarse-graining Z of its past, informational closure at every horizon is the same condition as zero one-step transfer entropy from the micro past, Barnett and Seth's dynamical independence, and as causal closure, Z's ε-machine coinciding with its υ-machine; for a coarse-graining of the present state it also makes Z's causal states a coarse-graining of X's, which does not imply closure, and the closed coarse-grainings are not closed under common refinement | Rosas et al. (arXiv 2024), [LIT-1306](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1306.md), read in [NOTE-1030](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1030.md), with Barnett and Seth's definition ([LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md)). For discrete stationary processes, the information-theoretic criterion of emergent closure (dynamical independence), the interventionist one (the macro's own causal states are all the micro distinctions that matter for it) and, for maps of the present state, a computational one are nested as stated. The first two are one condition. It says nothing about approximate closure. It does not make closure a mark of unity. "Causal" is only in the Granger sense unless X is fully observed. | Active |
